You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2016 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 25 [6 marks]: With reference to a business you have studied, analyse the relationship between cost and quality in the operations of the business.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 6):
6 marks: Draws out and relates the implications of the relationship between cost and quality with reference to a business
5 marks: Provides links between cost and quality with reference to a specific business
4 marks: Provides characteristics and features of cost and quality with reference to a business OR | Provides links between cost and quality in operations
3 marks: Provides characteristics and features of cost and/or quality
2 marks: Sketches in general terms cost and/or quality
1 marks: Makes reference to cost/quality

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Cost and quality usually have a close, positive relationship in the operations of a business. As the quality of a product increases, usually the cost of producing it also increases, as it requires more expensive inputs and/or more time to produce. An implication of this is that these products tend to have higher prices as businesses pass higher costs onto consumers. For example flights on low cost budget airlines such as Jetstar are cheaper to produce than flights on full-service flights such as those sold by QANTAS. Jetstar is less flexible and has fewer 'extras' such as food, entertainment and therefore provides a lower quality product, which is usually sold at a lower price.




STUDENT RESPONSE:
